subject.title: fix(cron): detect ===DONE_ERR=== sentinel in agent final text as failure signal

question: Should an isolated cron job's arbitrary terminal visible text beginning with `===DONE_ERR===` become a supported authoritative fatal-failure contract, or must failure remain an explicit structured signal from the execution boundary?
rationale: This choice changes persisted status and alerting semantics for existing jobs and cannot be resolved safely from resolver tests or the reporter's convention alone.

options.title: Require structured failure signals
options.body: Keep final visible text for presentation and have the agent-execution boundary emit the existing structured failure signal when the run actually fails.

options.title: Adopt a documented sentinel contract
options.body: Explicitly define producer ownership, escaping/false-positive behavior, upgrade semantics, and live end-to-end proof before allowing the sentinel to control cron state.

recommendation.title: Require structured failure signals
recommendation.body: Keep final visible text for presentation and have the agent-execution boundary emit the existing structured failure signal when the run actually fails.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the only supplied production evidence and can clarify the producer-side convention, though current-main code ownership still needs maintainer routing.
